notes: Each test case simulates a realistic coding task to validate docs-context skill behavior.
Fixtures (files/) represent starting project state; the eval runner should copy them into the agent's workspace before each run.
The agent under test has access to Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep tools and the docs-context skill.
Observable signals per run: (1) transcript (Skill invocations, tool calls, replies); (2) filesystem diff of docs/; (3) sync summary text if written.
Run each test twice: with docs-context skill available / without it. Compare pass rates and token cost.

Priority 1 (P1) tests cover the NEW behaviors introduced by the 2026-04-17 optimization (net-delta trigger, reverse rollback sync, no-op on design). These are the highest-risk and highest-signal tests.

evals.prompt: Add a /ping endpoint to the pay service that returns {"status": "ok"}. Use the existing controller pattern.
evals.expected_output: A /ping endpoint is implemented in the pay service, AND the agent auto-invokes docs-context Write Mode to update docs/modules.md with the new endpoint, AND emits a Doc Sync Summary all BEFORE the final task-completion reply. No user prompt to sync was given.
evals.setup_note: Fixture is a minimal pay service with existing docs/modules.md, docs/coding.md, and one controller. No /ping endpoint exists yet.
assertions: A /ping endpoint implementation exists in the pay service source files after the run.
The agent invoked the docs-context skill's Write Mode (visible as Skill tool invocation in transcript).
docs/modules.md contains a new entry for the /ping endpoint under the pay service after the run.
The transcript contains a section labeled 'Doc Sync Summary' (or Chinese equivalent '文档同步摘要').
Write Mode was invoked before the agent's final task-completion reply, not after.
The final task-completion reply acknowledges docs were synced.

evals.prompt: 给 pay 服务加个 /ping 接口吧，返回 {"status": "ok"} 就行
evals.expected_output: Same behavior as eval 1 but triggered via casual Chinese phrasing. The agent auto-invokes Write Mode without an explicit sync request.
evals.setup_note: Same fixture as eval 1. This tests prompt-style robustness — the agent must trigger on informal CN request just as reliably as on formal EN request.
assertions: A /ping endpoint implementation exists after the run.
The agent invoked docs-context Write Mode without being asked by the user.
docs/modules.md contains a new /ping entry.
Write Mode was invoked before the final reply.

evals.prompt: For rate limiting on our API gateway, compare approach A (token bucket in Redis) vs approach B (in-memory sliding window per-instance). Which do you recommend and why?
evals.expected_output: The agent provides a reasoned comparison and recommendation. NO code changes are made. NO docs are modified. Write Mode is NOT invoked (this is pure design discussion — syncing now would pollute docs if the design is later rejected).
evals.setup_note: Any fixture with existing docs will do. The key test: does the agent refrain from syncing when only analysis occurred?
assertions: The agent's reply contains a comparison of approach A vs B.
No files under docs/ were modified during the run.
No source code files were modified during the run.
The agent did NOT invoke docs-context Write Mode.
No 'Doc Sync Summary' appears in the transcript.

evals.prompt: Explain how the pay service handles transaction rollbacks. I want to understand the flow.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the code, explains the transaction rollback flow, and replies with a clear explanation. No files are modified. Write Mode is NOT invoked (read-only task).
assertions: The agent's reply contains an explanation of transaction rollback flow.
No files were modified during the run (neither source nor docs/).
The agent did NOT invoke docs-context Write Mode.
No 'Doc Sync Summary' appears in the transcript.

evals.prompt: Remove the /ping endpoint from the pay service — we're deprecating it. Clean up the code and any references.
evals.expected_output: The /ping endpoint code is removed, AND the agent auto-invokes Write Mode to REMOVE the /ping entry from docs/modules.md (reverse sync — docs must stay consistent with code). The Doc Sync Summary reports the removal under 'Updated'.
evals.setup_note: Fixture is pay service WITH /ping endpoint implemented AND documented in docs/modules.md. This is the critical rollback scenario: the entry was synced previously, and must now be removed to stay consistent.
assertions: The /ping endpoint code no longer exists in the pay service after the run.
docs/modules.md no longer contains a /ping entry after the run.
The agent invoked docs-context Write Mode.
The Doc Sync Summary mentions removing the /ping entry from modules.md.
No orphan references to /ping remain in other docs (e.g., architecture.md if it previously mentioned /ping).

evals.prompt: Add a new notification module with: (1) a NotificationService class, (2) a REST controller with POST /notify, (3) a Kafka consumer for 'notification.events' topic, (4) a DB migration adding a notifications table, (5) a config entry for kafka topic name. Use the existing patterns.
evals.expected_output: All 5 changes are landed across 5+ files. Write Mode is invoked EXACTLY ONCE at the end of the task, producing a single Doc Sync Summary covering all 5 changes.
evals.setup_note: Multi-file task. Critical assertion: Write Mode must not fire per file.
assertions: All 5 code artifacts exist after the run (NotificationService, controller, Kafka consumer, migration, config).
The agent invoked docs-context Write Mode exactly 1 time during the run (count skill invocations in transcript).
The single Doc Sync Summary references all affected document types (modules.md, tech-stack.md or architecture.md as applicable).
Write Mode was invoked after all 5 file changes, not between them.

evals.prompt: Try adding a 'createdBy' field to the Order entity, then actually no — revert that, keep the entity unchanged. Instead, just add a log statement in OrderService.createOrder that logs the caller's IP.
evals.expected_output: The Order entity is unchanged at task end (net zero there). Only the log statement in OrderService is added. Write Mode fires once and reports only the log statement change — NOT any Order entity change (which was tried and reverted within the task).
evals.setup_note: Tests that try-and-undo within a task leaves no net delta for that file. Only landed changes should appear in the sync summary.
assertions: The Order entity source file has no 'createdBy' field after the run.
OrderService.createOrder contains a new log statement referencing the caller's IP.
The agent invoked docs-context Write Mode.
The Doc Sync Summary does NOT mention any Order entity field change.
The Doc Sync Summary either (a) reports no module change if log additions don't affect modules.md, or (b) reports only a logging-related note.

evals.prompt: I've just added the /ping endpoint to pay service (files already written). Please do a pre-commit doc sync check.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects the already-made code changes (inspecting git diff or file state), invokes Write Mode based on the user's explicit signal, and updates docs accordingly.
evals.setup_note: Fixture: pay service has /ping code but docs/modules.md does NOT yet mention it. Simulates user coming back post-coding to sync.
assertions: The agent invoked docs-context Write Mode in response to the user's sync request.
docs/modules.md now contains a /ping entry.
The Doc Sync Summary acknowledges the endpoint addition.

evals.prompt: Add an Order refund endpoint POST /orders/{id}/refund that calls the existing RefundService.
evals.expected_output: Before coding, the agent invokes docs-context Read Mode to load at least docs/coding.md (always-load rule) plus task-appropriate docs (architecture.md + modules.md + tech-stack.md for 'new feature' + API design task type).
assertions: The agent invoked docs-context Read Mode before making code changes (Read Mode skill invocation or Read tool call targeting docs/coding.md appears in transcript).
The transcript shows docs/coding.md being read.
The transcript shows at least one of {docs/modules.md, docs/architecture.md} being read.
A /orders/{id}/refund endpoint implementation exists after the run.

evals.prompt: There's a bug in OrderService.createOrder — when the order amount is zero, it throws a NullPointerException instead of a validation error. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes Read Mode for a bug-fix task, loading docs/coding.md (always) + docs/modules.md (per task type). It does NOT load architecture.md or tech-stack.md (not required for bug fix).
evals.setup_note: Fixture: OrderService has the described NPE bug.
assertions: The agent read docs/coding.md during the run.
The agent read docs/modules.md during the run.
The agent did NOT read docs/architecture.md (per Read Mode scope rule for bug fixes).
The agent did NOT read docs/tech-stack.md.
The bug is fixed (the zero-amount case now throws a validation error, not NPE).

fixtures_needed.name: fixture-synced-pay

fixtures_needed.name: fixture-synced-pay-with-ping
fixtures_needed.description: Same as above, plus a /ping endpoint in source AND a /ping entry in docs/modules.md under pay service.
fixtures_needed.purpose: Used for rollback reverse-sync test (eval 5). The /ping entry must be documented for the rollback scenario to be meaningful.

fixtures_needed.name: fixture-synced-pay-with-new-ping-code
fixtures_needed.description: Same as fixture-synced-pay, plus /ping endpoint in source but NOT yet in docs/modules.md.
fixtures_needed.purpose: Simulates post-coding pre-sync state for user-triggered sync test (eval 8).

fixtures_needed.name: fixture-synced-pay-with-bug
fixtures_needed.description: Same as fixture-synced-pay, but OrderService.createOrder contains the NPE bug when amount is zero.

fixture_setup_instructions.how_to_create: Fixtures can be assembled as minimal Java/Go/Node projects. Suggested: copy a small real subproject, strip to 10-20 files, seed docs/ per templates in skills/docs-context/assets/templates/.
